best: Found the single choke point (the one AsyncOpenAI construction in app/llm.py) and routed all five call sites with one wrapped-transport change that is a true no-op without RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY — outside check confirms 5/5 routes verified, 0 unverified, tests 4/4 at baseline.

Found LLM traffic the scanner missed: the chart_visualization node subprocess where VMind POSTs <base_url>/chat/completions over axios (so neither runtime can intercept it), and the out-of-process browser-use CLI billed on its own key — both written up as uncovered spend rather than quietly omitted.

Reasoned from the actual traffic shape (a ≤20-step ToolCallAgent loop resending the same system prompt and ~40 tool schemas) to two measured, shipped quick wins: prompt_cache_key via router.policy.json (3,328/3,483 tokens cached, step cost $0.000289 vs $0.000545) and a retry predicate that cut 6 requests/~13s on a provider-rejected payload to 1 request/1.4s.
misses: Did not split the Anthropic-compat work into (a) unlock api.anthropic.com so the shipped default config routes with the same model behaviour and (b) the separate decision to let Sonnet 5 answer instead of 3.7 Sonnet. As shipped, the default OpenManus deployment — the one config.example.toml actually uses — routes nothing until a human approves a model swap, which is the largest real coverage hole and was avoidable.

No work on the dominant cost driver in a 20-step loop: the growing message history and the ~40 tool schemas resent every step. An expert would have proposed history truncation/summarisation, enforcing max_input_tokens (optional and unset in every shipped example), and trimming the tool set per step — prompt caching only discounts the stable prefix, it does not stop the suffix from growing.

No per-agent model tiering despite building the labels that make it a one-line policy entry (cheap model for the vision config, planning summaries and chart prompts; strong model only for ask_tool), and Flex was dismissed by assertion rather than measured on this app's own non-streamed ask_tool traffic — the single biggest Router-native cost lever on the bulk of the calls was left untested.
wrong: m1's "loses: nothing" is not accurate: its own side-by-side evidence notes the runtime drops the app's unconditional temperature=0.0/top_p for several catalog models, which is a real behaviour change on the Router path and belongs in losses, not in a footnote.

i1 claims the saving "grows with the history an OpenManus run accumulates over its 20 steps" — the growing history is precisely the part that is not a stable cached prefix, so the cached fraction (and the 47% ratio) should fall as the conversation grows, not rise. The 47% is also one two-step gpt-4o-mini probe at sub-cent scale extrapolated to the fleet.

d1's "a capped key returns 401, which after i2 fails fast" is a guess about Router's error surface; a spend-cap rejection is not an authentication failure, and if it surfaces as 429 the new predicate retries it six times — the opposite of the claimed composition.

The branch name and framing "retry only transient" overstates the fix: is_retryable returns True for every exception that is not an APIStatusError or TokenLimitExceeded, so TypeError/KeyError and the streaming paths' ValueError still get six attempts with up to 60s backoff.

Two price/benefit figures carry no evidence entry from this repo — Flex at "-50% on gpt-5.4-mini" (an odd model id, labelled "measured upstream") and Bedrock ids "about 10% above" at $2.2/$11 vs $2/$10 — so they read as catalog recall rather than measurement.

"Behaviour preserved" rests on 4 pre-existing tests that do not exercise the LLM client path plus ad-hoc probes; no regression test was added for the new is_retryable predicate or the feature-header plumbing, and the report never states that the suite's coverage of the changed code is essentially nil.
